independent_analytic_reasoning: For u=(-phi_y,phi_x), div(u dot grad u)=2phi_xy^2-2phi_xx phi_yy. Adding2partial_xu2 and using omega=phi_xx+phi_yy yields q=2phi_xx(1-omega)+2phi_xx^2+2phi_xy^2. Curl((1+d)gradPi)=d_xPi_y-d_yPi_x, with the negative of this expression on the vorticity right-hand side.

With z=x-tv, V=partial_yv=1+V1 and DL=partial_v-tpartial_z, partial_x=partial_z and partial_y=VDL. Thus Delta=partial_z^2+V^2DL^2+Vpartial_vV DL and V2=Vpartial_vV1. The transformed bracket gains exactly V. The mean identity H=tVpartial_vV3=-V1-f0 follows by differentiating the time-averaged shear and using meanomega=-partial_ymeanu1; it gives the stated V1,H transport equations.

Theorem1.1 quantifies beta0 first, then beta1 and the smallness threshold. The Gevrey exponent is1/2; finite first absolute y-moment and zero circulation are operative. Transport of initially small d preserves1+d>0 and hence positive density1/(1+d).

The mean obeys baromega(t,y)=f0(t,v(t,y)), with no tpartial_z derivative on that mode. The fixed Gevrey lower bound supplies H10 for f0 and bounded derivatives of V1. Repeated chain rule places the f0 derivative in L2 and the finitely many coordinate factors in Linfinity; the bounded positive Jacobian changes variables. This gives ||baromega||H10<=C_delta epsilon1.

The exact linear diagnostic w=epsilon cos(x-ty)exp(-y^2/2) has transport residual0, zero horizontal mean and constant sheared profile. Gaussian even moments give the displayed degree20 squared tenth-derivative polynomial with leading coefficient1, hence full derivative norm grows as t^10. This is only a linear coordinate diagnostic, not a nonlinear Euler counterexample.

For k!=0, D=k^2+(xi-kt)^2=k^2< t-xi/k >^2 and the toy inverse multiplier has magnitude k^2/D^2. Small V1,V1^2,V2 weighted coefficients are absorbed in Lemma3.5; density products in Lemma3.4 require both zero and nonzero modes. Averaging the vertical momentum equation gives partial_y[mean(phi_x^2)+meanPi]+mean(dPi_y)=0 and hence3.61. Lemma3.8 then yields mean-gradient <=C epsilon1^2+C epsilon1 sqrt(Ep+Bp). Combining the bootstrap, nonzero absorption and the Fourier Theta identity gives Ep+Bp<=C_delta(epsilon1^4+Etheta+Btheta). This is conditional on the stated product estimates, not a proof of every multiplier case.

For Q=k^2+|xi|, T=1+t^2 and b=sqrt(1+Q/T), bprime/b=-tQ/[T(T+Q)]<=0. Splitting Q into its two terms and bounding by min(1,k^2/T)+min(1,|xi|/T) yields the source's bounds by <k>^1/2/<t>^3/2+<xi>^1/2/<t>^2 and thus the small-sigma0 comparison with the base weight derivative. The extra derivative is never discarded.

Source p9 already bounds both F1 and F2 by Cepsilon1^2<t>^-3 in a fixed Gevrey norm. Uniform composition with a fixed radius loss preserves this decay. Integrating gives meanu1-uinfinity=O(<t>^-2); the exact identity partial_tv=t^-2 integral_0^t s partial_smeanu1 ds has bounded integral because integral s<s>^-3 ds is finite. Keeping only printed2.34 would instead give a logarithm. The stronger displayed estimate is the necessary existing repair.

Reference v1 Lemma4.2 uses only the appropriate bootstrap energies, weighted product estimates, ANR<=min(AR,A0), H=1-Vprime-meanf and the Neumann expansion of1/Vprime at this point. Matching Vprime-1 to V1 and Vdot to V3 checks the local algebraic transfer to source Lemma2.2. The profile right-hand sides have the stated integrable t^-2 decay after radius loss conditional on the global bootstrap, yielding t^-1 scattering tails.
